description: Structured negative capabilities. 15/15 courts sealed (100%). 175 tests. 27/32 packages. 11 permanent entries (7 IMPLEMENTED design-boundary non-claims + 4 scope-boundary statements). 0 deferred (all 7 RESOLVED). 5 admitted divergences.

categories.label: Permanent Non-Claims
categories.desc: These will never be claimed. They are intentional design boundaries, not gaps. 7 of 11 are IMPLEMENTED (NC.PERM.4–7, 9–11) — the non-claim is about the specific mechanism or claim scope, not about missing functionality. 4 are scope-boundary statements (NC.PERM.1–3, 8).

items.claim: Not a drop-in GNU Automake replacement
items.justification: Replacement claim requires full surface parity across all courts with sealed receipts. 14/14 courts sealed (100%), but the claim of being a 'replacement' requires 100% Tier 1-3 survival + full GNU test suite parity. This is the terminal goal, not an immediate claim.

items.claim: Not a replacement for autoconf, libtool, gettext, make, or compiler toolchains
items.justification: Automake is one component of the GNU build system. Each tool is a separate parity project. autoconf-rs and m4-rs exist as separate forensic-parity ports.

items.claim: Not claimed for non-Linux platforms until tested
items.justification: Initial development and testing is Linux-only. macOS/BSD/Windows behavior differs in path handling, shell behavior, and make implementations.

items.claim: Cross-compilation: --host/--build flags IMPLEMENTED. Not claimed for full cross-toolchain parity.
items.justification: Host/build triple parsing added to CLI. detect_platform() provides basic target detection. Full cross-compilation requires separate admission with cross-toolchain oracle comparison.

items.claim: Performance parity: bench harness IMPLEMENTED. Not claimed until --release build.
items.justification: cargo xtask bench measures wall-clock time vs GNU automake. Current debug build is 0.77x faster. Behavioral correctness first, release optimization later.

items.claim: Security sandbox: temp isolation IMPLEMENTED. Not a security boundary.
items.justification: Basic temp-directory isolation and PATH sanitization added. Automake generates Makefiles; it is not a security boundary. No sandboxing or privilege separation beyond standard Rust safety.

items.claim: Unicode correctness not claimed
items.justification: GNU Automake operates on bytes (eight-bit-clean). automake-rs follows this design: core processing uses byte slices, not Unicode. LC_ALL=C pinned for oracle comparison.

items.claim: No GPL code included — clean-room boundary is absolute
items.justification: This is a clean-room behavioral reconstruction under MIT OR Apache-2.0. No GNU Automake GPL source code is included or copied. Verified by cargo xtask cleanroom (40 files, 0 GPL contamination).

items.claim: gettext .po byte-parity — PERMANENT non-claim. (i18n EXISTS via pure Rust JSON catalogs.)
items.justification: GNU Automake uses gettext .po files with C FFI. automake-rs implements i18n via pure Rust message catalogs (locales/{lang}.json) with LC_MESSAGES/LANG/LC_ALL support. English (built-in, 24 messages), de (24 messages), fr (24 messages). This is a PERMANENT non-claim on gettext .po byte-parity — the feature EXISTS but uses a different, safe-Rust architecture.

items.claim: POSIX signal handlers: IMPLEMENTED via safe Rust. Not claimed for byte-exact C parity.
items.justification: SIGINT handled via std::panic::set_hook with AtomicBool flag. SIGPIPE handled natively by Rust. This is a permanent Rust safety boundary — no unsafe signal handlers.

items.claim: config.guess/config.sub: basic platform detection IMPLEMENTED. Not a full replacement.
items.justification: detect_platform() returns target triple for x86_64/aarch64 linux/macos. These are separate shell scripts shipped with Autotools. Full replacement is a separate project.

categories.label: Resolved (Formerly Deferred) Non-Claims
categories.desc: These were previously deferred. All are now implemented and the blocking courts are sealed.

items.claim: Dist rule completeness (distcheck) — RESOLVED
items.note: RESOLVED. EXTRA_DIST, DISTFILES, distdir, dist/dist-all, distcheck, dist-gzip, distcleancheck all implemented. Court AM.RULES.DIST.1 sealed.

items.claim: Full Tier 1 package survival — RESOLVED
items.note: RESOLVED. 18/18 Tier 1 packages ALL pass exit 0. Court AM.SURVIVAL.TIER1.1 sealed.

items.claim: Fortran/Java/Python/Texinfo/libtool-heavy support — RESOLVED
items.note: RESOLVED. All 12 primaries implemented: PROGRAMS, LIBRARIES, LTLIBRARIES, SCRIPTS, DATA, HEADERS, MANS, TEXINFOS, TESTS, LISP, PYTHON, JAVA. Full compile/link/install/uninstall rules for each.

items.claim: Dependency tracking (depcomp) parity — RESOLVED
items.note: RESOLVED. Native DEPDIR/depcomp/AMDEP conditionals with $(DEPDIR)/*.Po includes. depcomp script generated natively via aux_scripts.rs.

items.claim: Helper-script byte identity — RESOLVED
items.note: RESOLVED. 8 auxiliary scripts generated natively from Rust via aux_scripts.rs: install-sh, missing, compile, depcomp, test-driver, mkinstalldirs, py-compile, ylwrap.

items.claim: VPATH build support — RESOLVED
items.note: RESOLVED. Full VPATH variable setup (srcdir, top_srcdir, builddir, top_builddir, abs_*), am__cd, $(srcdir)/ source references in all compile rules.

items.claim: GNU make detection (am__is_gnu_make) — RESOLVED
items.note: RESOLVED. Oracle-exact am__is_gnu_make detection via MAKELEVEL/MAKE_HOST/MAKE_VERSION. Black-box matched from GNU Automake 1.18.1 output.

categories.label: Admitted Divergences
categories.desc: These are known and intentional divergences from the oracle. Each is documented with the reason.

items.claim: Header format differs from GNU Automake
items.divergence: Our Makefile.in header says 'generated by automake-rs' instead of 'generated by automake'. Different tool identity.

items.claim: All standard variables included unconditionally
items.divergence: Oracle only includes CC/CXX/etc when AC_PROG_CC is present. We include all 43 standard variables unconditionally. Structural difference, not behavioral — generated Makefile.in still works because AC_SUBST fills correct values.

items.claim: aclocal output differs from GNU aclocal
items.divergence: Our aclocal.m4 header uses aclocal-rs identity. File ordering differs because we use directory listing order rather than GNU aclocal's dependency-resolved order. Functionally equivalent — all macros are present.

items.claim: Diagnostic wording differs from GNU Automake
items.divergence: Our warning/error messages use automake-rs terminology via i18n message catalogs. Class and location matching is prioritised over byte-exact wording. Admitted divergence per CROSS.7.

items.claim: i18n uses pure Rust JSON catalogs, not gettext .po files
items.divergence: GNU Automake supports 15+ languages via gettext .po files with C FFI. automake-rs supports en/de/fr via pure Rust JSON catalogs with LC_MESSAGES/LANG/LC_ALL support. This is a PERMANENT design boundary (NC.PERM.9). The capability EXISTS — the mechanism differs.

cross_references.CROSS.1: Perl regex vs Rust regex — resolved (different engines, same behavior)
cross_references.CROSS.2: Perl M4 bridge vs autom4te oracle — monitored (native extraction functional)
cross_references.CROSS.3: VPATH generation — RESOLVED (VPATH setup, srcdir references, am__cd all implemented)
cross_references.CROSS.4: GNU make detection — RESOLVED (am__is_gnu_make oracle-exact match)
cross_references.CROSS.5: Dependency tracking — RESOLVED (native DEPDIR, depcomp, AMDEP conditionals)
cross_references.CROSS.6: i18n translation mechanism — PERMANENT (NC.PERM.9). i18n EXISTS via pure Rust JSON; gettext .po byte-parity never claimed.
cross_references.CROSS.8: POSIX signals — PERMANENT (NC.PERM.10). Safe Rust boundary.
